nasa.title: Preparing users for satellite missions before launch
text: At NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, Brown led the pre-launch applications programs for two Earth-observing missions: the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, launched in 2015, and the Ice, Cloud and land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2), launched in 2018. Both programs paired prospective users — agencies, companies and researchers — with mission scientists years before the first data arrived, through Early Adopter programs, workshops and user-needs assessments.

She continues to lead the ICESat-2 applications team, and has studied the programs' results: a review of the ICESat and ICESat-2 literature found that engagement of stakeholders accelerated applications of ICESat-2 data compared with its predecessor.

impact.title: Satellite evidence in famine early warning
impact.text: For more than a decade Brown ensured that USAID's Famine Early Warning Systems Network had access to — and used — real-time and projected vegetation and rainfall data for Africa, Central America, Afghanistan and Haiti, and evaluated how those data entered early-warning assessments.

impact.title: Climate change and the U.S. food system
impact.text: Lead author of the USDA technical report Climate Change, Global Food Security, and the U.S. Food System, prepared for the U.S. National Climate Assessment. The writing team received the USDA Abraham Lincoln Honor Award for Increasing Global Food Security (2016).

impact.title: Climate and children's diets
impact.text: A nineteen-country study she co-authored associated climate impacts with reduced diet diversity in children; it was reported by the BBC and Forbes, among others.

evidence.label: Niles et al. (2020), Environmental Research Letters

impact.title: Advising the National Academies
impact.text: Member of the National Academy of Sciences Committee on Earth Science and Applications from Space (2017–2022), and earlier of the National Science Foundation's Environmental Research and Education Advisory Committee (2010–2012).
